prior_full.problem: Let $G$ have $p_c(G)=1$. For percolation on $G\times\mathbb Z$, must every infinite cluster intersect each fiber $\{v\}\times\mathbb Z$ it meets in infinitely many vertices a.s.? (Saint-Flour, Open Problem.)
prior_full.status_literature: Listed as open. No resolution found.
prior_full.work_done: Web + arXiv search; no resolution located.

original_two_entries.route: Deferred-decision capped exploration and propagation across adjacent fibers
original_two_entries.result: No infinite cluster has uniformly bounded fiber intersections when p_c(G)=1; any infinite fiber intersection propagates to every fiber. General finite-but-unbounded fiber sizes are not excluded.

original_two_entries.route: Uniform cutset reduction and variable-cap extension
original_two_entries.result: The known cutset theorem is strictly stronger: an exponentially stretched binary tree has p_c=1 but no uniform cutset bound. An inhomogeneous percolation on a ray demonstrates why edge bounds approaching 1 do not contradict homogeneous p_c=1. No original-target counterexample or full proof.
